Happy New Year R-users!

Marissa Baskett and I would like to announce the following ECL298 for the upcoming quarter, Winter 2013:

Course title: Computational methods in population biology
ECL 298, CRN: 50354 (3 units, graded as S/U)

Course Description:
Numerical methods for simulating population dynamics using the computational software package R. An emphasis will be placed on model formulation and development, theoretical concepts and philosophical principles to guide simulation efforts, and implementing simulations with R. Topics covered may include simulation of difference/differential equations, matrix & continuously structured models, stochastic difference equations, and discrete/continuous-time Markov processes. Applications covered include structured population dynamics, spread of diseases, spatial spread of invasive species, population viability analysis, time series analysis of species interactions, and metapopulation and metacommunity dynamics.

Pre-requisites: a course in theoretical ecology (e.g., PBG 231 or an equivalent to ESP 121 from your undergraduate institution) or consent of instructor; no programming experience required.

Time: Mondays at 12:10-2:00pm plus an optional (but highly recommend) lab of structured work time on Fridays at 12:10-2:00pm, both in Wickson 2124. Note: The online scheduler incorrectly is reporting Tuesday as a meeting time. 

Instructors: Marissa Baskett and Sebastian Schreiber

Attached is a syllabus for the course. 

Please let Sebastian (sschr...@ucdavis.edu) or Marissa (mlba...@ucdavis.edu) know if you have any questions.
